Misleading Subscription Renewal Date & Refund Refusal. I had a very disappointing experience with this company’s subscription renewal process.

I received an email stating that my membership would renew on May 21, so I canceled my subscription on May 21, believing I was doing so at the renewal date. However, I later discovered that my payment had actually been processed on May 20, one day earlier than the date provided in their email.

When I contacted customer support to request a refund, they refused, explaining that the charge was processed based on a different time zone and that cancellations must be made at least 24 hours before renewal. The problem is that none of that was clearly communicated in the renewal email. If customers are told they have until May 21, they should reasonably be able to cancel on May 21 without already being charged.

This feels misleading and lacks transparency. If the actual deadline is the day before due to time zone differences or a 24-hour cancellation policy, that information should be stated clearly in the renewal notice.

I’m sharing this so other customers know to cancel well in advance, regardless of the renewal date shown in the email. I hope the company updates its communication to make the process more transparent and fair.

Not helpful postpartum. The method of this app only works if you take your temperature after you wake up but before you get out of bed at about the same time every day after a “normal” night of sleep. When you’ve just had a baby, you’re not going to lay in bed and take your temp for a minute when you’ve woken up to your baby crying. There is no “normal” night of sleep anymore. And I certainly don’t wake up at the same time these days. Even if you use an oura ring that takes your temperature automatically, you could be awake with the baby at the scheduled time and it will impact your temp reading. 

Lastly, there is no way to get the little notification badge to go away. Even if you’ve already logged your temp for the day and read every info tip and article they send you, you will STILL have a little red “1” notifications over the app icon. Which might drive you nuts if you’re a certain type of person.

App content: App resource library has pro-morning after pill resources and links to emergency contraceptives. The app article claims the pills do not end a pregnancy but it would be more accurate to say they prevent implantation (vs fertilization) which would still considered abortifacient. 
Ease of use: I had the thermometer and started using this app in postpartum mode and then birth control. Because I have a little one who is a poor sleeper I rarely had an uninterrupted 4 hour stretch of sleep before waking up (recommended by the app for getting accurate data). They did come out with the band but for $99 at the discount price (and my previously mentioned ethical concerns) I didn’t want to spend that. I’m sure if I had been able to provide data more consistently, I would have trusted the predictions more. 
Reimbursement process: When I joined, they said my specific insurance should cover it (they had a whole feature to check coverage with different insurance providers), so I paid the subscription and submitted a reimbursement claim with my insurance. It got rejected, I pushed back and finally got it taken out of my deductible but no reimbursement. Then they changed to say it should be covered under your Rx insurance. I never tried that but I noticed they’ve now changed it to say HSA/FSA will reimburse you. Maybe they will and maybe they won’t. Again, haven’t tried. At this point I’m not sure I would trust Natural Cycles on their reimbursement promises. 
Final thoughts: if you are pro-life, I would suggest finding a different app. Natural Cycles medical advisory board includes a medical professional who has actively helped develop abortion medication. This indicates a bias towards abortive methods and as someone who believes human life is sacred (including unborn human life), this is problematic for my moral convictions. A Game-Changer for My PCOS and Fertility Journey ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐. As someone with PCOS and a history of fertility struggles, I've tried nearly everything to regulate my cycle and understand my body better. But nothing has been as life-changing as the Natural Cycles app. I honestly can't express how much this app has helped me not only track my cycles but also get a clearer picture of my fertility something I never thought I'd truly understand.
With PCOS, my periods are irregular, and for years, I felt like I was just guessing when I was ovulating or whether I was even ovulating at all. Natural Cycles has taken all the guesswork out of it. The temperature-based tracking, combined with their algorithm, has given me a real-time understanding of my cycle. I now know exactly when I'm most fertile, which has been key for us as we try to conceive.
But what I really love is the way Natural Cycles helps me feel in control. It’s not just a generic fertility app it’s personalized. The app learns about my cycle and adjusts the predictions based on my unique data. No more wondering if my body is acting "normally" for PCOS I can see it all laid out clearly.
The ability to track my basal body temperature (BBT) every day, along with other symptoms, has made a huge difference in how I approach my health. I’m no longer reliant on guesswork or feeling overwhelmed with conflicting advice. The app’s educational resources have also been invaluable in helping me understand my body better, something I’ve struggled with for years.
Additionally, I really appreciate how safe and effective the app is for birth control, too. I’ve been using it for both contraception and fertility tracking, and I trust it completely. I feel like I finally have a tool that works for my body, rather than trying to fit my irregular cycle into traditional methods that just weren’t made for me.
Overall, Natural Cycles has been a total game-changer in my fertility journey. Whether you’re dealing with PCOS or any other fertility issues, I can’t recommend this app enough. It has empowered me in ways I never thought possible, and I feel more connected to my body than ever before.

A Great Option!. This app is such a great option for women who are in search of a non invasive alternative to hormonal birth control!
That being said it is not for everyone and if you are deciding if it might work for you I recommend to take these things into consideration: 
1) There is notably more personal responsibility involved when using NC as birth control, but on the flip side it puts you completely in control of your reproductive health. 
2) This is not a passive method and you have to make sure you’re getting as many temperatures as possible, tracking your menstruation, and (though not required but definitely helpful) taking LH tests when the app suggests. 3) You also have to be comfortable enough with your partner to be able to communicate which part of your cycle you’re in and what that means for your method of protection on that day. 
4) I will also note that I found the experience was much smoother using a wearable (apple watch) to track my temperatures than when I was using the thermometer. But whatever tracking method you use you just have to be very consistent. 
I love the app and it has really benefited me at this stage in my life- but hormonal birth control also has its benefits and I’m glad I was on it during more turbulent phases of my life like when I was a student or when I was not in a committed relationship with someone I trusted. Consider discussing with your doctor before making your decision because even though it works great for me it might not be right for you!

I had a fairly consistent cycle, 31 days on the spot, until one day… I didn’t. Absolutely nothing changed in my lifestyle, but my cycle decided it wanted to be 25 days, and if it weren’t for extreme diligence, I would be pregnant right now (in fact, I think I was, but that’s another story). The app said I was “green” well beyond when my period ended, and even past my ovulation frame. It took the “data”from my last 12+ cycles, so when I would have just been ending my period, I was actually ovulating, and the app had zero idea (because how could it?) Again, if I hadn’t been aware of what was going on, I would have no idea, and would have just gone with what the app was telling me. If you’re cycle changes in the slightest, an app isn’t going to catch that in time for you to take the appropriate action. I’m not sure how people go multiple years on this method without being paranoid every month that they’re pregnant. I couldn’t do the mental game anymore, and would rather just take the effects of hormonal birth control than the utter mental distress of think I was pregnant every month. If you’re ready/in the stage of life to have kids, sure, I suppose this would work. Otherwise, I just don’t see how relying on an app will work when you have no say in how long or short your cycle will be. Just be warned!

A Non-Hormonal Birth Control Journey. After 8 years on hormonal birth control pills followed by 1.5 years with a hormonal IUD, I made the decision to transition away from synthetic hormones in early 2024. This choice was driven by growing awareness of how hormonal contraception can influence factors such as libido and even partner preference topics that are often overlooked in mainstream discussions.

Since removing my IUD in February 2024 and switching to Natural Cycles, the experience has been nothing short of empowering. The app’s integration with my Ōura Ring has allowed me to track my fertility with remarkable precision. Monitoring my “green” (non-fertile) and “red” (fertile) days has not only provided a reliable method of birth control but has also deepened my understanding of my overall health and cycle patterns.

Natural Cycles stands out as the only FDA-cleared digital birth control that is completely hormone-free. It offers a non-toxic alternative to traditional methods, eliminating the need for hormonal intervention. For those seeking a more natural and informed approach to reproductive health, I highly recommend exploring this option.

Overall, this transition has helped me feel more in tune with my body and more confident in my bodily autonomy. Natural Cycles has proven to be both effective and enlightening.

If you are new to basal body temp tracking (which is what this app is) please note that if you sleep irregularly (like you're taking care of a small child or infant as A LOT of us are) it is almost impossible to get an accurate read on your temperature with the thermometer. This will make it harder for the algorithm to predict your cycle and it will likely be much less accurate than someone who sleeps 8hrs straight. You would need the invest in the tech and subscriptions for the apple watch or aura ring to make it more accurate. 

Waking up throughout the night makes it hard to know when to take your temperature, and unless you want to be checking the clock and counting the hours in your head at 3AM and taking your temp this method will probably drive you crazy like it did for me. 

The sign up process is a headache, they ask you tons of questions but nowhere in all of that do they mention this type of monitoring is HARD for irregular sleepers or even what to do if you're waking several times a night.

I understand policies exist. But ethical businesses don’t hide behind them when it’s clear a customer isn’t trying to game the system and is just asking for fairness.

Natural Cycles may work for a small subset of people, but it’s built on incredibly rigid input requirements that are incompatible with many women’s real lives. And if it doesn’t work for you, don’t expect a shred of empathy or basic decency from their customer service.

Great way to track. I’ve had this app for a little over a year and a half. Getting off of hormonal birth control and choosing to track my cycle has been the best choice I’ve made. I highly recommend this app for anyone wanting to escape the traditional birth control route.
Random price increase. They jacked the price up for their subscription and didn’t add or change anything in the app. Fraud, utilize free apps instead of this.

Customizable Trackers Please!. The app is great except it is misleading in that it makes you believe you can track ovulation with temperature alone. You also need to be tracking at least cervical fluid or cervical position as well. There have been times when it says I’m not fertile but I still have very clear ovulatory cervical fluid indicating otherwise.

Also, I wish there was a way to customize trackers. I’d love to be able to create my own things to track within the app besides what’s offered.

10/10 recommend!. This app has changed my life for the better! I had been on hormonal birth control for 14 years and knew basically nothing about my body and how it was supposed to operate naturally. Natural Cycles has given me knowledge, confidence, and power over my own body. I will NEVER go back to hormonal birth control!
Price!!. It would be better if they lowered the price a little bit. I think for what it does it shouldn’t be 20 monthly. But overall a really good app.

reviews.text: Mainly chaotic and triggering.. I purchased this app when TTC after a loss because it touts robust tracking features using data and science. I also track with other apps, and both provided WAY more accurate results than NC. Not only that, I find it odd that when planning a pregnancy the days you CAN get pregnant are RED, because they treat every user like they don’t want to get pregnant, which is odd and pretty limited IMO. The thermometer was also insanely stressful and super finicky, leading to so much constant fear. All in all, read the Reddit threads from other users and consider one of the many other apps out there for BC/ TTC.
